oracle_provenance: Fisher (1921) r-to-z transformation, standard textbook inferential statistics; independently hand-verified before implementation. Not copied from any shared Skill fixture.
scope: Bounded statistical-support check for a claimed metric-to-MOS correlation; not a computed MOS prediction itself.

cases.question: Does a strong claimed correlation at a reasonably large sample size produce a confidence interval that excludes zero (statistically supported)?
At the minimum sample size and a weak claimed correlation, does the confidence interval span zero, correctly showing the claim is not yet statistically supported?
Must a claimed correlation of exactly +/-1 (undefined under Fisher's transform) be rejected rather than silently used?
For the identical claimed correlation, does a larger sample size narrow the confidence interval (as the model's own math guarantees), discriminating a genuine sample-size effect from noise?
